indian.headline: Indian markets closed lower as DIIs booked profits and inflation concerns weighed on sentiment.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed lower as DIIs booked profits and inflation concerns weighed on sentiment.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.39%, Nifty 50 dropped 0.61%, and Bank Nifty slid 0.79% as selling pressure across sectors outweighed buying.
why: Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) sold ₹47,662 crore over nine sessions—their longest selling streak in four years—triggering broad-based profit-taking across the indices.
Retail inflation hit 6.09% in October, exceeding the RBI's 4% comfort zone, signaling the central bank may raise interest rates further, which pressures equities and bonds alike.
Banking and IT sectors fell 0.8% and 0.7% respectively on rate-hike anxiety; metals and autos also sold off (−1.0% and −1.1%) as growth concerns deepened.
Heavy selling pressure on Indian government bonds ahead of fresh debt supply amplified the bearish mood across risk assets including equities.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities closed in the red on 13 November as profit-booking by domestic funds and surging inflation concerns overwhelmed the market. The Sensex fell 0.39%, Nifty 50 dropped 0.61%, and Bank Nifty weakened 0.79%, with losses spread across nearly all sectors. Financials and IT—normally the market's backbone—led the retreat, signaling investor anxiety over the prospect of higher interest rates.

The core trigger was inflation: retail prices rose to 6.09% in October, breaching the RBI's 4% upper tolerance limit for the first time in months. This sparked fresh rate-hike bets and heavy selling in government bonds ahead of debt auctions, creating a risk-off mood. Compounding this, DIIs—domestic institutional investors—were in the midst of their longest selling streak in four years, offloading ₹47,662 crore over nine sessions. While foreign funds returned and the government approved a ₹62,370-crore fertiliser subsidy for farmers, these supports proved insufficient to reverse the day's downward momentum.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: Foreign funds returned to India, but global rate-hike concerns persist.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: Foreign funds returned after a period of selling; DIIs offloaded ₹47,662 crore.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: No fresh price data; Energy sector unchanged at +0.0%.

indian.watch: Monitor RBI's rate-hike signals and tomorrow's bond auction outcome—they will set the tone for equities.

us.headline: US markets closed lower as Nvidia leadership chaos overshadows AI sector optimism.
us.lead: US markets closed lower as Nvidia leadership chaos overshadows AI sector optimism.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 0.35%, Nasdaq dropped 0.39%, and Dow shed 0.36% in a broad selloff.
why: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation threatens a $500 billion AI infrastructure financing deal, spooking Wall Street confidence in the company's stability and leadership.
Tech sector weakness (-0.3%) and financials decline (-0.7%) dragged main indices lower, offsetting energy gains (+1.5%) from traditional sectors.
Nvidia stock crashed to its longest losing streak since 2012, losing $1.6 trillion in value, causing retail panic selling despite Cerebras surging 17% on Microsoft deal news.
us.narrative:
US markets ended in the red on 13 November as Nvidia's leadership turmoil cast a shadow over Wall Street's AI bets. CEO Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation and interim CFO Colette Kress stepping in created uncertainty around a $500 billion AI financing deal involving six major Wall Street firms. The broader tech sector (-0.3%) and financials (-0.7%) fell, though energy stocks rallied 1.5%, unable to support the indices. Healthcare also declined 0.6%.

The AI sector showed cracks despite positive news elsewhere. Cerebras jumped 17% after beating earnings and announcing a Microsoft partnership, signalling strength outside Nvidia. Take-Two Interactive's strong Q2 bookings of $1.6 billion and over $1 billion in GTA VI pre-sales provided gaming momentum. Meanwhile, Cognizant's CFO warned that AI agents could handle 40% of client work, adding uncertainty to IT services hiring. Retail investors, historically patient during crashes, are buying Nvidia's dip as the stock faces its worst streak in years.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: AI chip makers diverge sharply on Microsoft deal and earnings strength.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: GTA VI pre-sales exceed $1 billion one week before launch.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Leadership crisis at Nvidia shakes confidence in AI infrastructure spending.

us.watch: Will Nvidia stabilise under interim CFO or does leadership vacuum trigger the $500 billion financing deal collapse?
